key_insight: Large language models can automate reproducibility checks in the social and behavioral sciences, closely matching original study conclusions and outperforming human reanalysis on qualitative agreement.
engineering_relevance: This suggests LLM pipelines can scale audit workflows for empirical research, enabling faster and more systematic reproducibility screening with minimal manual effort.
method: Evaluated 76 published studies with predefined claims from the social and behavioral sciences.
Used an LLM pipeline to reconstruct analyses and compare recovered effect sizes and conclusions against originals.
Benchmarked LLM performance against human reanalysts on effect-size recovery and qualitative agreement.
evidence_signal: The LLM pipeline recovered original effect sizes in 41% of studies and matched the original qualitative conclusion in 96% of cases, versus 34% and 74% for human reanalysis, respectively.
watch_item: The pipeline failed to produce a viable effect size estimate for 7 studies, so edge cases and analysis ambiguity remain important implementation concerns.
paper_title: Automated reproducibility assessments in the social and behavioral sciences using large language models
